propositions: The snapshot janitor's 2 GiB absolute free-space watermark is disk-size-blind and crossed only at 93.3% used on a 30 GiB volume, above both the 85% alarm floor and the observed 90% peak.
Every review materializes a full ~620 MiB copy of the ticket tree keyed on a ref advancing every ~26 seconds, causing ~4.4 GiB/hour growth on the root disk where REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR is unset.
The janitor's reclaim triggers are structurally unreachable: the 2 GiB absolute floor cannot engage before the alarm fires, and the 7-day cold-trim exceeds the container lifetime of hours.

The fix adds a volume-relative free-watermark term (free_watermark_pct as whole integer percent of volume) that scales the trigger below the alarm floor on small volumes, with hysteresis to avoid re-firing every interval.
Reclaim now engages at 80% used instead of never, engaging before the 85% alarm floor and preventing review-bot health dips from disk exhaustion.
The byte-total backstop promised by ADR 0005 is not implemented in _gc_pass, and materialize_tickets never calls add_bytes, leaving the dominant consumer byte-accounted at zero.
